sample_unit: emergency radiology reports (dataset 1); 200 reports stage 1, 100 stages 2-3, 800 stage 4

links.outcome: Error detection rate of LLM versus radiologists of different seniority on same reports
links.effect: DeepSeek-R1 few-shot 84.4% vs residents 51.6% and 53.1% (both P<.05); no significant difference vs senior/attending radiologists (68.8%-93.8%, P=.26 to ≥.99).
links.quote: Its performance exceeded that of radiology residents (84.4% vs 51.6% and 53.1%, respectively; both P<.05) and showed no statistically significant difference compared with senior radiologists and attending radiologists (84.4% vs 68.8%-93.8%, P=.26 to ≥.99).

links.outcome: Real-world validation of LLM error detection on verified reports
links.effect: In real-world validation on 800 reports, DeepSeek-R1 identified 117 true reporting errors, positive predictive value 56.5%.
links.quote: In real-world validation, DeepSeek-R1 identified 117 true reporting errors, yielding a positive predictive value of 56.5%.

links.effect: In dataset 2 from independent institutions, DeepSeek-R1 achieved a detection rate of 95% under the few-shot setting.
links.quote: In dataset 2, collected from independent institutions, DeepSeek-R1 achieved a detection rate of 95% under the few-shot setting.

unlisted_practices: Few-shot prompting versus 0-shot prompting to improve LLM error detection (84.4% vs 60.9%, P=.003)
Using LLM as assistive proofreading tool for radiology reports

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM performance (DeepSeek-R1) for detecting errors in emergency radiology reports compared to radiologists across retrospective datasets, without evaluating an organizational deployment safeguard or practice intervention.
